name: CalculateWatermarksMALLUseAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport
prose: Static void function that takes the scratch area and a parameter struct p, returns nothing, and has no early return and no goto; it runs straight through to the end. It writes the watermark fields of p->Watermark (Urgent, USRRetraining, DRAMClockChange, FCLKChange, StutterExit, StutterEnterPlusExit, Z8StutterExit, Z8StutterEnterPlusExit) from the latencies in p->mmSOCParameters, and the writeback watermarks: WritebackLatency, plus p->WritebackChunkSize*1024/32/SOCCLK when more than one surface has WritebackEnable set, plus USRRetrainingLatency when USRRetrainingRequiredFinal is set. For each active surface k it computes latency-hiding margins from line-buffer lines and DET buffering, subtracts the watermarks (the writeback margins are cross-wired: the DRAM margin is min-ed with the writeback FCLK margin and the FCLK margin with the writeback DRAM margin), and writes p->MaxActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencySupported[k] (0 for a phantom-pipe surface), p->ActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencyMargin[k] and p->SubViewportLinesNeededInMALL[k] (the larger of the luma and chroma line counts only when BytePerPixelDETC[k] > 0). It sets *p->USRRetrainingSupport to true and then to false if any non-phantom surface has a negative USR retraining margin. It writes *p->MaxActiveFCLKChangeLatencySupported only when at least one non-phantom surface exists (the minimum of FCLK margin plus FCLKChangeLatency over them); otherwise that location is left as it was. It writes *p->FCLKChangeSupport (vactive, vblank or unsupported) and *p->DRAMClockChangeSupport (vactive, vblank, vblank_drr, with the _w_mall_full_frame or _w_mall_sub_vp variants when any surface uses full-frame or sub-viewport MALL, or unsupported) from the margins, PrefetchMode, DRR flags and the synchronization relation between surfaces. Many intermediate values are stored in the scratch locals struct. Divisions by DCFClkDeepSleep, SOCCLK, PixelClock, HTotal, VRatio, SwathWidth and LBBitPerPixel are not guarded, so the caller must supply nonzero values.
note: slice cut the head (real head at display_mode_core.c:2822, named CalculateWatermarksMALLUseAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport, not CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport); prior rejection 'name not in slice' was right; prior prose also described fields differently and said nothing of the cross-wired writeback margins (lines 2953-2954). R:right

name: CalculateOutputLink
prose: Static void function with no return statements and no goto. It first sets *RequiresDSC and *RequiresFEC to false, *OutBpp to 0, *OutputType to dml_output_type_unknown and *OutputRate to dml_output_rate_unknown, and does nothing more when IsMainSurfaceUsingTheIndicatedTiming is false or when Output is not HDMI, DP, DP2.0 or eDP (*RequiredSlots untouched in those cases). For HDMI it sets *OutputType to dml_output_type_hdmi and *OutBpp to the result of TruncToValidBPP(min(600,PHYCLKPerState)*10, 3 lanes, ...) with a local dummy in place of RequiredSlots; *RequiresDSC and *RequiresFEC stay false and *OutputRate stays unknown. For DP, DP2.0 and eDP it sets *RequiresDSC true when DSCEnable is dml_dsc_enable (and *RequiresFEC true for DP and DP2.0 in that case), otherwise *RequiresDSC false and *RequiresFEC true only for DP2.0. It then tries link-rate tiers in order (UHBR10, UHBR13p5, UHBR20 for DP2.0; HBR, HBR2, HBR3 for DP and eDP), each tier only if OutputLinkDPRate is dml_dp_rate_na or that rate, the PHY clock is large enough, and (for tiers after the first) *OutBpp is still 0. In a tier it calls TruncToValidBPP with the downspread-adjusted rate, passing RequiredSlots as an output, and when that gives 0, DSCEnable is dml_dsc_enable_if_necessary, ForcedOutputLinkBPP is 0 and (for the lower tiers) the PHY clock is below the next tier's threshold, it sets *RequiresDSC true (and *RequiresFEC true for DP, not for eDP, in the HBR tiers) and calls TruncToValidBPP again. When a tier is entered it sets *OutputType (dml_output_type_dp2p0, dml_output_type_dp or dml_output_type_edp) and *OutputRate for that tier, so they keep the value of the last tier entered and stay unknown if no tier condition held (then *OutBpp is 0 as well).
note: slice started mid-function; real head at display_mode_core.c:5341. Reviewer claim 2 (OutputType stays unknown when no rate-tier condition holds) is right (lines 5377-5378, types set only inside tier branches at 5419, 5433, 5446, 5464, 5481, 5498); original claim (HDMI OutputType is hdmi, RequiredSlots not written for HDMI) is right too (5387, dummy at 5385). R:right

name: dml_core_mode_programming
prose: Non-static void function (display_mode_core.c:8291-9912) taking the mode library state and a clock configuration; it has no return statement inside the body and no goto, so it runs straight through. It first derives the active plane and pipe counts and the pipe/plane mapping from mode_lib->ms.cache_display_cfg and stores them in mode_lib->ms and mode_lib->mp, and sets locals->Dcfclk to mode_lib->ms.DCFCLK unless clk_cfg->dcfclk_option is dml_use_override_freq, in which case it takes clk_cfg->dcfclk_mhz. It then fills the programming results in mode_lib->mp (display, DPP and DSC clocks with required or override frequencies per clk_cfg option, read bandwidths, swath/DET configuration, DCFCLK deep sleep, DSC delays, MALL surface sizes, and further prefetch, watermark and stutter values by calling the helper functions) and uses the shared scratch area for temporary parameter structs. The returned information is in mode_lib->mp; there is no return value. The slice given covers only the part from the dispclk calculation through the DSCCLK calculation. Many divisions in the body (HTotal, PixelClock and similar) are not guarded.
note: slice cut the head (enclosing function is dml_core_mode_programming starting at display_mode_core.c:8291, which is 1620+ lines); prose is deliberately general because only part of the body is summarised. No return/goto in the whole function (checked). R:n/a

name: CalculateStutterEfficiency
prose: Static void function (dml2_core_dcn4_calcs.c:10072-10359) that takes the internal scratch and a params struct p, returns nothing and has no return or goto. It zeroes its locals struct with memset, then over the non-phantom surfaces accumulates total compressed, zero-size-request and row read bandwidths (with a per-surface maximum compression of 2 or 4 chosen from block size and DCC uncompressed block limits for DCC surfaces), derives AverageDCCCompressionRate and AverageDCCZeroSizeFraction from p->TotalDataReadBandwidth and the compressed total (divisions are not guarded), and computes an effective compressed buffer size by one of three formulas depending on whether the zero-size fraction is 1, above 0, or 0. It sets *p->StutterPeriod to the minimum DET buffering time over non-phantom surfaces (0 if there is none) and records that critical surface's frame time, active time and sizes. It writes *p->StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank, *p->Z8StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank and the two burst counts as 0 when any non-phantom stream has an active writeback and otherwise from the SR exit times, the burst time and the stutter period; it then writes *p->StutterEfficiency and *p->Z8StutterEfficiency (equal to the not-including-vblank value unless timings are synchronized or there is one OTG with the same timing, and 0 with a burst count of 0 when that value is 0), and *p->DCHUBBUB_ARB_CSTATE_MAX_CAP_MODE. All outputs go through pointers in p.
note: slice cut the head (real function CalculateStutterEfficiency starts at line 10072; slice began inside it); 'pure arithmetic' prior prose also hides the scratch memset and output pointers. Note the writeback test at 10273 indexes stream_descriptors[k] with the surface index k instead of the stream index; kept out of the prose. R:n/a

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Static function (dml2_core_dcn4_calcs.c:5102-5940) taking the internal scratch and a params struct p and returning a bool. It sets s->NoTimeToPrefetch to false at entry, computes trip and dynamic-metadata timing values (writing s->TWait_p, s->LineTime, *p->Tvm_trips, *p->Tr0_trips, the flip variants, *p->Tdmdl_vm, *p->Tdmdl, *p->NotEnoughTimeForDynamicMetadata and the VUpdate/VReady offsets through CalculateVUpdateAndDynamicMetadataParameters) and the DPP and DISPCLK cycle counts. There are two returns. At line 5246 it returns true immediately if p->myPipe->Dppclk or p->myPipe->Dispclk is 0.0, before writing *p->DSTXAfterScaler, *p->DSTYAfterScaler and the later prefetch outputs. Otherwise it continues through the prefetch bandwidth and line-count computations and, at line 5939, returns s->NoTimeToPrefetch, which is true when the computation found there was not enough time to prefetch (in which case the prefetch outputs dst_y_per_vm_vblank, dst_y_per_row_vblank, dst_y_prefetch, VRatioPrefetchY/C, the required prefetch pixel-data bandwidths and prefetch_vmrow_bw are reset to 0) and false otherwise. The function does not always return true.
note: slice cut the head (real function begins at 5102). The previous prose said it always returns true, which is wrong: line 5246 returns true early for Dppclk/Dispclk zero and line 5939 returns s->NoTimeToPrefetch. Prior rejection 'name not in slice' was a slice problem. R:right

name: math_log2_approx
prose: Returns 0 when a is 0 or 1; for a greater than 1 it returns the number of times a can be shifted right by one before it reaches 1 or less, which is floor(log2(a)) and at most 31. The parameter is a by-value copy that the loop shifts, so the caller's variable is unchanged; no memory, locks or globals are touched. The loop terminates for every unsigned int input.
note: Prose already correct (lib_float_math.c:132-140, single return at 139). Reviewer objections were all about the formal contract (uses modified parameter a, unbound result, signed 1<<31 overflow), which are right for the old contract text; contract left empty because the post-state of a (it is shifted down to 0/1) makes any contract that mentions a ambiguous. R:right

name: dpp401_dscl_set_scaler_manual_scale
prose: Void function (dcn401_dpp_dscl.c:1052-1186) that programs the DSCL scaler and line buffer in manual scaling mode from scl_data. It compares the cached dpp->scl_data with *scl_data using memcmp and returns at once with no register writes when they are byte-equal. If scl_data->dscl_prog_data.isharp_en is set and the cached sharpness_level differs, it programs the isharp delta filter, copies the new sharpness level and the isharp_delta table into the cache, and returns if the cache now equals *scl_data; otherwise it sets program_isharp_1dlut to true. It then replaces the cache with *scl_data. When config.use_spl is set and debug.disable_spl is clear it takes dscl_mode, recout, MPC size and tap counts from scl_data->dscl_prog_data. When debug.enable_mem_low_power.bits.dscl is set and the mode is not DCN401_DSCL_MODE_DSCL_BYPASS it powers on the DSCL. It writes DSCL_AUTOCAL (off), DSCL_CONTROL boundary mode 0, recout, MPC_SIZE and SCL_MODE. For DSCL bypass it powers the DSCL off if the low-power debug flag is set and returns. Otherwise it picks an LB memory config and sets the line buffer; for DCN401_DSCL_MODE_SCALING_444_BYPASS it disables EASF if config.prefer_easf is set, programs isharp and returns. In the remaining modes it writes the black offsets if the SCL_BLACK_OFFSET register exists, sets manual ratio and init values, the tap control, programs isharp, sets the SCL filter, and programs EASF if config.prefer_easf is set. It returns nothing and reports no error. After the cache is replaced, every return leaves dpp->scl_data equal to *scl_data.
note: slice cut the head: the packet slice starts inside dpp401_dscl_set_scaler_manual_scale (head at line 1052); the old name dpp401_dscl_program_scaler does not exist in this file. Old prose otherwise matched the code (returns at 1073, 1088, 1135, 1146, end). R:n/a

name: dcn401_update_bandwidth
prose: Returns bool. It calls dc->res_pool->funcs->validate_bandwidth(dc, context, DC_VALIDATE_MODE_AND_PROGRAMMING) and returns false right away if the result is not DC_OK, before calling prepare_bandwidth (validate_bandwidth itself may change the context). Otherwise it calls dc->hwss.prepare_bandwidth(dc, context) and loops over all pipes in context->res_ctx.pipe_ctx up to the pool pipe_count. Pipes whose plane_state is NULL are skipped. For a pipe with a plane_state and no top_pipe it programs the timing generator global sync (vready offset for the group, vstartup, vupdate offset and width, pstate keepout) and VTG params, calls hws->funcs.blank_pixel_data(dc, pipe_ctx, blank) when prev_odm_pipe is NULL (blank is true when is_pipe_tree_visible is false, so this can blank or unblank), and calls setup_vupdate_interrupt if that hook exists. For every pipe with a plane_state (top pipe or not) it then calls hubp_setup2 with the pipe's hubp_regs, global_sync and stream timing if that hook exists. It returns true at the end. The pipe's stream_res.tg, stream and plane_res.hubp pointers are dereferenced without checks.
note: Checked against dcn401_hwseq.c:2404-2455. Reviewer claim (precondition omits stream validity for non-top pipes using hubp_setup2) is right: line 2451 reads pipe_ctx->stream->timing for any pipe with plane_state. Earlier reviewer claim (skips NULL plane_state pipes) was already covered by the old prose. R:right

name: construct_phy
prose: Static bool (link_factory.c:454-758) that fills in a struct dc_link for a physical connector from the BIOS object table. It sets irq sources to DC_IRQ_SOURCE_INVALID, copies dc, ctx and link_index, clears the preferred training and link settings, gets the connector id from the BIOS and sets ep_type to DISPLAY_ENDPOINT_PHY. Returns false (via create_fail) when the object type is not OBJECT_TYPE_CONNECTOR, when the connector id is an eDP and smart mux is configured while dc_edp_id_count is already non-zero, or for an unsupported connector id. It optionally calls the resource pool link_init hook, gets and opens the HPD gpio (interrupt mode, unlocks the pin) when one exists, sets connector_signal and the HPD/HPD-RX/read-request irq sources by connector type, creates the ddc service, sets ddc_hw_inst, creates the link encoder via the pool's link_enc_create, records eng_id in res_pool->link_encoders[] and increments dig_link_enc_count, sets link_enc_hw_inst, and for eDP/LVDS creates a panel controller if the pool has panel_cntl_create (incrementing dc_edp_id_count whether or not creation succeeds). It then loops up to 4 times calling get_device_tag; a failing call jumps to device_tag_fail, while a loop that finds no matching tag simply ends and keeps the last tag read. It optionally copies channel mapping, chip caps and forced drive settings from bios->integrated_info, calls get_atom_dc_golden_table if present, calls program_hpd_filter, sets PSR version to unsupported and returns true. Failure labels cascade: device_tag_fail destroys the link encoder (but not its entry in res_pool->link_encoders and not the incremented count) and falls through; link_enc_create_fail destroys panel_cntl if non-NULL; panel_cntl_create_fail destroys the ddc service; ddc_create_fail and create_fail (reached directly) do not destroy the ddc service, so a ddc service created but lacking ddc_pin is not destroyed there; all failure paths destroy the hpd gpio irq and clear hpd_gpio when it exists, and return false. The panel_cntl_create_fail path does not destroy the link encoder.
note: slice cut the head: the packet slice sits inside construct_phy (head 454), not a function called construct_link (link_construct at 829 is a different small wrapper). Old prose was close to the code; checked each goto (499, 547, 588, 602, 608, 629, 657, 665) against labels at 741-749. R:n/a

name: dp_handle_hpd_rx_irq
prose: Returns bool and handles a DP short-pulse (HPD RX) interrupt on a link. At entry it sets *out_link_loss and *has_left_work to false when those pointers are non-NULL, reads the IRQ data with dp_read_hpd_rx_irq_data and copies it to *out_hpd_irq_dpcd_data (if non-NULL) even when the read failed. Return paths in order: false if the DPCD read did not return DC_OK; false after an AUTOMATED_TEST request (it clears the AUTOMATED_TEST bit in the device service IRQ vector by a DPCD write, then either defers the work by setting *has_left_work when defer_handling is set and has_left_work is non-NULL, or runs the automated test handler directly); false if dp_should_allow_hpd_rx_irq says no (no established lane count and not a branch device); true if handle_hpd_irq_psr_sink reports a PSR error was handled; true if UP_REQ_MSG_RDY is set (deferred via *has_left_work when requested); false if DOWN_REP_MSG_RDY is set. Otherwise, for non-eDP signals, if link loss is parsed from the IRQ data it defers via *has_left_work or calls dp_handle_link_loss, sets the result to false and sets *out_link_loss true; if DP tunneling is supported and the tunneling IRQ bit is set it calls dp_handle_tunneling_irq; and for an SST branch link whose reported sink count differs from link->dpcd_sink_count it sets the result to true (this can override a false set by link loss). The final return is that result, true only when a sink-count change was seen on an SST branch.
note: slice started at line 512 inside dp_handle_hpd_rx_irq (head at link_dp_irq_handler.c:410); the item was dropped for 'name not in slice'. Old prose (returns true when sink count changed, reports link loss via out parameters) is incomplete but not contradicted: the true returns at PSR and UP_REQ are not sink-count changes. R:n/a

name: perform_link_training_with_retries
prose: Returns bool and runs DP link training with retries and optional fallback to lower link settings. It copies link_setting into the current and maximum settings, sets up the stream encoder for 8b/10b, and loops while j < attempts and fail_count < attempts*10 (so it returns false without any attempt when attempts is 0 or less). Each iteration enables the link PHY with the current settings, optionally sleeps for the sink's dppowerup_delay, sets the panel mode and ASSR, then: if link->aux_access_disabled, it runs AUX-less training and returns true at once without checking a status. Otherwise it trains (through dpia_perform_link_training for a USB4 DPIA endpoint when consolidated_dpia_dp_lt is not set, else dp_perform_link_training) and returns true if the status is LINK_TRAINING_SUCCESS and is_link_bw_low is false; before that return, a USB4 DPIA endpoint with an MST stream has link->verified_link_cap updated and dm_helpers_dp_mst_update_branch_bandwidth called. A failed attempt increments fail_count. For a DISPLAY_ENDPOINT_PHY endpoint the loop is left with a break, before dp_disable_link_phy is called, when this was the last attempt or the status is LINK_TRAINING_ABORT, so the PHY stays enabled on that path and the function returns false. Otherwise the PHY is disabled; for LINK_TRAINING_ABORT it then breaks (returning false, PHY already disabled) if link_detect_connection_type reports dc_connection_none. If the attempt is not retried at lower bandwidth (do_fallback false, abort, success with low bandwidth, or minimum RBR x 1 already) it increments j, resets the settings to link_setting and lengthens the delay; otherwise it picks a fallback with decide_fallback_link_setting and recomputes is_link_bw_low and is_link_bw_min. It sleeps between attempts. After the loop it returns false.
note: Checked against link_dp_training.c:1618-1815. Reviewer claims: (a) PHY stays on at final failed PHY-endpoint attempt (break at 1729 before 1755), right; (b) sink-unplug abort disables PHY before break (1755 then 1763) and success also needs !is_link_bw_low, right; (c) omitted false return on sink-unplug break before limits, right. All three round-1/2/15 claims were valid against the older prose. R:right

name: dp_perform_fixed_vs_pe_training_sequence
prose: Returns enum link_training_result and trains an 8b/10b DP link through a fixed-VS/PE vendor retimer. If lt_settings->lttpr_mode is LTTPR_MODE_NON_TRANSPARENT it returns at once the status from perform_fixed_vs_pe_nontransparent_training_sequence (which raises cr_pattern_time to at least 16000, applies the vendor link-rate toggle workaround, writes link settings, and runs clock recovery and channel equalization per repeater from the repeater count down and then for DPRX, stopping at the first non-success). Otherwise it sets pre_disable_intercept_delay_ms from debug.fixed_vs_aux_delay_config_wa (1x for 2 repeaters, 2x for more than 2, 0 otherwise), sends vendor reset, vs, pe and intercept-enable writes to the retimer, writes DP_DOWNSPREAD_CTRL and DP_LANE_COUNT_SET (enhanced framing; POST_LT_ADJ_REQ_GRANTED taken from the sink capability when pattern_for_eq is below pattern sequence 4), and, when the LTTPR OUI is all zero, writes a toggled link rate to DP_LINK_BW_SET if link->vendor_specific_lttpr_link_rate_wa equals the rate or is 0 and updates that field to the rate. It then writes the real rate to DP_LINK_BW_SET, sends the dpmf vendor writes (plus five more for four lanes), and runs a clock recovery loop (bounded by LINK_TRAINING_MAX_RETRY_COUNT and LINK_TRAINING_MAX_CR_RETRY, with up to 10 intercept-disable attempts on the first pass) and sets status from dp_get_cr_failure. If that status is success it runs the channel equalization loop with the vendor eq writes, where the status becomes LINK_TRAINING_EQ_FAIL_CR if clock recovery is lost, LINK_TRAINING_SUCCESS when ch_eq, symbol lock and interlane alignment are all done, and stays LINK_TRAINING_EQ_FAIL_EQ when the retry count is exhausted. It returns that status.
note: slice cut the head: the function defined here is dp_perform_fixed_vs_pe_training_sequence (link_dp_training_fixed_vs_pe_retimer.c:189-553), there is no function called dp_perform_fixed_vs_pe_retimer_link_training and the old prose's pre_disable_intercept_delay_ms parameter does not exist (it is a local). The earlier drop was for a missing name; fixing under the real name. R:n/a

name: core_link_read_dpcd
prose: Returns enum dc_status and reads size bytes of DPCD starting at address into data. It first calls dpcd_extend_address_range, which, if the requested range starts or ends inside the mandatory block from DP_LT_TUNABLE_PHY_REPEATER_FIELD_DATA_STRUCTURE_REV to DP_PHY_REPEATER_128B132B_RATES, widens it to cover that block and then allocates a temporary zeroed buffer with kcalloc (only an ASSERT checks for failure, so a NULL result is not handled); otherwise the buffer is data itself. It then reads partition by partition through internal_link_read_dpcd, splitting on the mandatory DPCD partition table (dpcd_get_next_partition_size searches the table and would run past it for addresses beyond the table). internal_link_read_dpcd returns DC_OK without reading when link->aux_access_disabled is set, and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED when dm_helpers_dp_read_dpcd fails; the loop stops at the first non-DC_OK status. When the range was extended, dpcd_reduce_address_range copies reduced_size bytes from the caller's data into the temporary buffer (the wrong direction) and frees the buffer, so the bytes read are not copied back to data and data is unchanged in that case. The return value is DC_OK if every partition read returned DC_OK (including all reads skipped because aux access is disabled, in which case data is not filled), DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED if a partition read failed, and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED without any read when the loop is not entered, which is the case for size 0 (even when aux_access_disabled is set). It keeps no references.
note: Checked against link_dpcd.c:44-57, 111-126, 138-195, 197-228. Reviewer claims: (1) copy-back goes the wrong way: right (line 193 memcpy(&extended_data[offset], reduced_data, ...)); (2) aux_access_disabled returns DC_OK without reading: right (50-56); (3) aux disabled with size 0 returns DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED: right (loop at 217 never runs). R:right

name: core_link_write_dpcd
prose: Returns enum dc_status and writes size bytes from data to DPCD at address, partition by partition. The loop runs while size is non-zero: it takes the next partition size from the mandatory DPCD partition table (dpcd_get_next_partition_size, which would run past the table for addresses beyond it), calls internal_link_write_dpcd, and stops at the first status other than DC_OK. internal_link_write_dpcd returns DC_OK without writing when link->aux_access_disabled is set and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED when dm_helpers_dp_write_dpcd fails. The result is DC_OK when every partition returned DC_OK (so with aux access disabled it returns DC_OK having written nothing), DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED when a partition write failed (partitions already written stay written), and DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED without any write when size is 0, even when aux_access_disabled is set. It keeps no references or locks.
note: Checked against link_dpcd.c:59-72, 230-250. All three reviewer claims right (size 0 returns DC_ERROR_UNEXPECTED at 238/240; aux disabled returns DC_OK without writing; both combined for size 0). R:right

name: edp_set_backlight_level
prose: Returns bool. It reads backlight_pwm_u16_16 and frame_ramp from backlight_level_params and logs them with DC_LOG_BACKLIGHT (a log call that executes on every path). If link->connector_signal is not an embedded signal (dc_is_embedded_signal) it does nothing else and returns true. For an embedded signal it looks up the pipe for the link with get_pipe_from_link, stores backlight_pwm_u16_16 in link->panel_cntl->stored_backlight_registers.USER_LEVEL when link->panel_cntl is non-NULL (this store happens before the pipe check, so it also happens on the false return), and returns false if no pipe is found. Otherwise it sets frame_ramp to 0 when the pipe's plane_state is NULL, writes the resulting frame_ramp back into backlight_level_params->frame_ramp, calls dc->hwss.set_backlight_level(pipe_ctx, backlight_level_params) and returns true.
note: Checked against link_edp_panel_control.c:550-583. Reviewer claims: USER_LEVEL write conditional on panel_cntl (right, 563), still written on the no-pipe false return (right, 563-573), and 'no side effects' for non-embedded is wrong because DC_LOG_BACKLIGHT always logs (right, 556-558). R:right

name: edp_set_psr_allow_active
prose: Returns bool and applies PSR settings to an eDP link. In order: returns false if the pool's psr (dmub_psr) is NULL and force_static is true; returns false if dc_get_edp_link_panel_inst fails; returns false if allow_active is non-NULL, *allow_active is true and link->type is dc_connection_none. If power_opts is non-NULL and differs from link->psr_settings.psr_power_opt it stores the new value and, when psr is non-NULL, psr_feature_enabled is set and the psr_set_power_opt hook exists, calls it. If psr is non-NULL, psr_feature_enabled is set, force_static is true and the psr_force_static hook exists it calls that hook. If allow_active is non-NULL and *allow_active differs from link->psr_settings.psr_allow_active it stores the new value, calls dc_z10_restore(dc) when the new value is false, then calls psr_enable when psr is non-NULL and psr_feature_enabled is set, else dmcu set_psr_enable when a dmcu exists, is initialized and psr_feature_enabled is set, else returns false (after the stored value and any z10 restore, power-option change and force-static call have already happened). Otherwise it returns true. psr_enable is called without checking that the hook pointer is non-NULL.
note: Checked against link_edp_panel_control.c:585-632. Reviewer claims: false path when no psr and no dmcu after allow_active changed (right, 629), that path has already stored psr_allow_active and may call dc_z10_restore (right, 618-621), and force_static also requires psr_feature_enabled (right, 612-613). R:right

name: dcn10_mpc_construct
prose: Void constructor (dcn10_mpc.c:498-520) that initialises a struct dcn10_mpc. It stores ctx in mpc10->base.ctx, sets mpc10->base.funcs to &dcn10_mpc_funcs, stores the register, shift and mask table pointers in mpc10->mpc_regs, mpc_shift and mpc_mask, sets mpc10->mpcc_in_use_mask to 0 and mpc10->num_mpcc to num_mpcc, and then for i from 0 to MAX_MPCC-1 calls mpc1_init_mpcc(&mpc10->base.mpcc_array[i], i). The loop count is MAX_MPCC regardless of num_mpcc. It returns nothing, has no failure path, and does not copy the tables (it keeps the pointers).

name: mod_hdcp_hdcp2_dp_transition
prose: Returns enum mod_hdcp_status and runs one step of the HDCP 2.x DisplayPort transition state machine with a switch on current_state(hdcp), filling the output callback and watchdog fields and setting the next state. name: amdgpu_od_set_init
prose: Static int (amdgpu_pm.c:4528-4660) that creates the gpu_od sysfs directory tree for overdrive controls. It allocates top_set with kzalloc and returns -ENOMEM immediately (no cleanup needed) if that fails; otherwise it adds top_set to adev->pm.od_kobj_list, creates its kobject named gpu_od under the device kobject (failure goes to err_out), and then, for each named container in amdgpu_od_set.containers: a self-contained container whose feature is not supported is skipped with nothing created; a supported self-contained container gets an od_attribute (linked into top_set->attribute, not into the od_kobj_list) and a sysfs file under gpu_od; any other container gets a sub_set added to adev->pm.od_kobj_list with a kobject named after the container under gpu_od, plus an od_attribute (linked into sub_set->attribute) and sysfs file for each supported sub_feature. Failures of kzalloc (-ENOMEM), kobject_init_and_add or sysfs_create_file jump to err_out, which calls amdgpu_od_set_fini(adev) and returns the error. Finally, if adev->pm.od_kobj_list holds only gpu_od (list_is_singular), it also goes to err_out, so amdgpu_od_set_fini removes everything and the function returns the current ret value, which is 0 at that point. Otherwise it returns 0. If kobject_init_and_add fails for top_set or a sub_set, that entry is already on the list but its attribute list head is not yet initialised, so amdgpu_od_set_fini, which walks the attribute list of every list entry, reads a zeroed list head there.

name: smu10_read_sensor
prose: Returns int. It decides has_gfx_busy: true for a Picasso APU with smu_version at least 0x41e3b or a Raven APU with smu_version at least 0x1e5500, false otherwise. AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_VCN_POWER_STATE stores 0 when vcn_power_gated is set and 1 otherwise, sets *size to 4 and returns 0. AMDGPU_PP_SENSOR_GPU_LOAD returns -EOPNOTSUPP when has_gfx_busy is false (so it is supported only on those firmware versions); otherwise it sends PPSMC_MSG_GetGfxBusy, stores min(activity_percent, 100) in *(uint32_t *)value and returns 0 on success, or returns -EIO if the message fails (it does not set *size). name: smu7_apply_state_adjust_rules
prose: Returns int. It returns -EINVAL immediately if cast_phw_smu7_power_state of request_ps->hardware is NULL; otherwise it returns 0 after adjusting the requested power state in place. It sets data->battery_state (true when the ui_label is PP_StateUILabel_Battery) and clears data->mclk_ignore_signal. Only when the AC flag adev->pm.ac_power is false does it clamp every performance level's memory and engine clock down to the DC maximums (max_clock_voltage_on_dc). It takes minimum clocks from the display configuration; when the StablePState platform cap is enabled it instead uses AC limits, sets the minimum engine clock to the highest vdd_dep_on_sclk entry not above 75 percent of the AC max sclk (or entry 0 if none), and sets the minimum memory clock to the full AC max mclk (not 75 percent). It then decides whether to disable mclk switching (frame-lock cap, or several unsynchronised displays, or a vblank that is too short); with no displays it sets mclk_ignore_signal on POLARIS10 through VEGAM chips and otherwise disables the no-switching condition. Level 0 gets the first level's clocks raised to the minimums (capped at the limit), and when switching is disabled on a chip outside POLARIS10..VEGAM the memory clock is taken from the last performance level (index performance_level_count - 1), not the second. Level 1's engine clock is raised to at least level 0's. With switching disabled it uses level 1's memory clock as a floor and, for POLARIS10..VEGAM with display-based disabling, searches the mclk latency table for the lowest frequency within the tolerable latency (setting mclk_ignore_signal if none qualifies), or uses level 1's memory clock for frame lock; with switching enabled it only raises level 1's memory clock to at least level 0's. With StablePState enabled every performance level is overwritten with the stable-pstate engine and memory clocks and with pcie_gen and pcie_lane both set to data->pcie_gen_performance.max.

name: analogix_dp_transfer
prose: Returns ssize_t and performs one DP AUX transaction through the Analogix DP controller registers. It returns -E2BIG (after a WARN_ON) if msg->size is above 16 and -EINVAL, before any further register access beyond the initial buffer clear, if the request (with DP_AUX_I2C_MOT masked off) is not one of I2C write, I2C read, native write or native read. It programs the command, length and 20-bit address registers and, when bit 0 of msg->request is clear (the write requests), writes msg->buffer bytes into the data registers. It sets AUX_EN (plus ADDR_ONLY for size 0) and polls for AUX_EN to clear (500 ms) and for RPLY_RECEIV (20 ms); on either timeout, or when an AUX error is flagged with a status other than timeout, it reinitialises the AUX channel with analogix_dp_init_aux and returns -EREMOTEIO. An AUX_ERR with AUX_STATUS_TIMEOUT_ERROR returns -ETIMEDOUT directly (without the reinitialisation). On success it copies msg->size bytes from the data registers into msg->buffer when bit 0 of msg->request is set (that is the I2C read and the native read), sets msg->reply to the native or I2C defer value if the RX command register shows a defer, otherwise to the I2C ACK or native ACK according to the request type, and returns msg->size.

name: sp_tx_edid_read
prose: Static int (anx7625.c:1122-1235) that reads the EDID through the AUX channel into pedid_blocks_buf. It writes the AUX address registers and returns -EIO if any of those register writes returns a negative value; returns the negative value of sp_tx_get_edid_block if that fails; then loops count from 0 while blocks_num >= count. For count 0 and 1 it reads eight chunks of MAX_DPCD_BUFFER_SIZE bytes with edid_read and copies each successful chunk into the buffer, stopping that inner loop at a failure (edid_read failure does not make the function fail, and the remaining chunks are not read for that count); for count 2 and 3 it reads eight chunks each with segments_edid_read and returns that function's negative value (an errno from the register, AUX or retry logic, not necessarily -EIO) as soon as one fails; other counts do nothing. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if drm_edid_is_valid fails on the buffer, returns the negative value of sp_tx_rst_aux if the final AUX reset fails (not necessarily -EIO), and otherwise returns blocks_num + 1, even if some edid_read chunk failed earlier but the buffer still passed the validity check. The buffer is written at offsets up to 32 chunks of MAX_DPCD_BUFFER_SIZE bytes, so it must be at least that large, and drm_edid_is_valid reads according to the block count in the data.

name: samsung_dsim_transfer
prose: Static int (samsung_dsim.c:1530-1564) that submits one DSI transfer and waits for it. It sets xfer->tx_done and rx_done to 0, xfer->result to -ETIMEDOUT and initialises the completion. Under dsi->transfer_lock (irqsave) it records whether the transfer list was empty and appends xfer; if the list was empty it calls samsung_dsim_transfer_start. It then waits for xfer->completed for DSI_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS (the return value of the wait is ignored). If xfer->result is still -ETIMEDOUT afterwards it calls samsung_dsim_remove_transfer to take the transfer off the list (starting the next queued one when the head was removed), logs the packet, and returns -ETIMEDOUT; otherwise it returns xfer->result, which also covers a hardware timeout reported by the interrupt handler. The caller keeps ownership of xfer.
note: slice cut the head: the function is samsung_dsim_transfer (head at samsung_dsim.c:1530); there is no unnamed_xfer_submit. Old prose consistent with the code. R:n/a

name: tc_probe
prose: Static int I2C probe function (tc358767.c:2456-2604) with many early error returns, each after devm-managed allocations that are released by the driver core. In order it picks the bridge funcs from tc_probe_get_mode, allocates tc with devm_drm_bridge_alloc (returns PTR_ERR on failure), calls tc_probe_bridge_endpoint (returns its nonzero error, covering panel or bridge lookup, panel bridge add and DPI probe failures), gets and enables the 'ref' clock (error returned through dev_err_probe), handles the optional shutdown and reset GPIOs (errors returned), initialises the regmap (error returned), reads the optional toshiba,hpd-pin property (hpd_pin becomes -ENODEV if absent; a value outside 0 to 1 returns -EINVAL), and when client->irq > 0 writes INTCTL_G and requests the threaded irq (failure returned, success sets have_irq). It reads TC_IDREG into tc->rev and returns the read error, or -EINVAL when the ID is neither 0x6601 nor 0x6603; sets assr for 0x6601; performs a software reset sequence if there is no reset GPIO; programs HPD counters and, if have_irq, enables the HPD interrupts when hpd_pin is valid; for non-DPI (eDP/DP) output calls tc_aux_link_setup and returns its error if nonzero. It then sets bridge.of_node, calls drm_bridge_add, stores tc as i2c clientdata, and for DSI input calls tc_mipi_dsi_host_attach; if that fails it calls drm_bridge_remove and returns the error via dev_err_probe, but the clientdata set before is not cleared. Otherwise it returns 0. Failures after drm_bridge_add other than the DSI attach cannot occur.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at tc358767.c:2456). Reviewer claims: DSI attach failure leaves clientdata set (right, 2593 vs 2598-2599), omits -EINVAL for hpd-pin and tc_aux_link_setup error (right, 2519 and 2585-2587), omits tc_probe_bridge_endpoint failures (right, 2473-2475). R:right

name: process_single_tx_qlock
prose: Static int (drm_dp_mst_topology.c:2792-2853) that sends one chunk of a sideband message; the caller is expected to hold mgr->qlock (the _qlock suffix). It returns 0 at once, sending nothing, when txmsg->state is already DRM_DP_SIDEBAND_TX_SENT. Otherwise it zeroes a local header, changes txmsg->state from QUEUED to START_SEND, and calls set_hdr_from_dst_qlock, which fills the header (broadcast with lct 1 and lcr 6 for connection-status-notify, resource-status-notify and clear-payload-id-table requests, otherwise lct/lcr and rad from txmsg->dst) and in the code shown always returns 0 (the early return of a negative value after it is therefore unreachable). It computes the bytes left, limits the chunk to 48 minus 1 CRC byte minus the header size, sets SOMT when nothing has been sent yet and EOMT when the whole remainder fits, encodes the header, copies the chunk, adds the CRC and calls drm_dp_send_sideband_msg on the down or up channel according to up. If that returns nonzero it optionally dumps the message and returns that value; txmsg->cur_offset is not advanced but txmsg->state has already moved from QUEUED to START_SEND. On success it advances cur_offset and returns 1 with state set to DRM_DP_SIDEBAND_TX_SENT if the message is complete, otherwise 0.
note: Checked against drm_dp_mst_topology.c:2763-2788 and 2792-2853. Reviewer claims: precondition names qlock not lock (right: the _qlock suffix and callers), returns 1 on completion and negative on send failure (right, 2850 and 2844), state may already have changed to START_SEND on failure (right, 2806-2807 happens before the send). R:right
